root_cause.text: The virt_wifi driver sets the net_device's parent to the lower device's `struct device` via `SET_NETDEV_DEV`, creating a dangling pointer when the lower device is freed during unregistration, which ethtool then accesses via `pm_runtime_get_sync(dev->dev.parent)`, causing a use-after-free.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explains that unregistering a virt_wifi device can happen concurrently with the referenced lower device, leaving `dev.parent` pointing to freed memory, and `ethnl_ops_begin()` calls `pm_runtime_get_sync(dev->dev.parent)`, triggering the KASAN report. The patch removes the `SET_NETDEV_DEV` line to break this parent link.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove assignment of parent device for virtual wifi net_device to avoid potential device hierarchy issues.
intent_record.what: Removed the call to SET_NETDEV_DEV(dev, &priv->lowerdev->dev) in virt_wifi_newlink, which previously set the virtual wifi net_device's parent to the lower device's device.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the virtual wifi net_device will no longer have its parent device set to the lower device. This affects device hierarchy in sysfs and may influence power management and other device relations.

relevance_review.reason: The group removes the SET_NETDEV_DEV assignment that sets the parent device, which directly addresses the root cause of the use-after-free by eliminating the dangling pointer.
